product: Email Security Gateway and Email Gateway Defense
author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: Two sources. Email Security Gateway appliance: set the syslog server under Advanced > Advanced Networking; the mail syslog's RECV, SCAN and SEND lines, one per action per recipient, go to Email with Barracuda's action and reason codes turned into names. Email Gateway Defense (Email Protection Advanced plan): set the syslog integration (TCP with TLS) to the data collector; message log records go to Email, with status, reason and threat taken from the first recipient. EGD audit records and the appliance's web syslog stay generic. A gateway status of DELIVERED on RECV and SCAN lines means the appliance let the message through; SEND lines carry the delivery result. SCAN and RECV lines use the Start epoch time; SEND lines use the header time, which has no zone and is read as UTC. Barracuda publishes the appliance's field order and code tables but no full example line, and EGD's syslog header isn't documented, so the parent reads EGD records from the email[1]: tag to the end of the line. EGD documents attachments only as null, so attachments aren't mapped. Samples are made up from Barracuda's field order and EGD's JSON examples. Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-13, and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there; the parent and children have not run together as separate parsers yet. No built-in parser in that tenant matched these lines.
